doc.title: Delfeayo Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Own band and New York period
title: Based in New Orleans; the Brewhouse gig
summary: Back in New Orleans he played a nine-month modern jazz gig on Decatur Street where management only wanted background music.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: After you graduated from Berklee, up until ’97, all this time from ’89 to ’97, you’re still based in New Orleans. Is that correct?

Yes. I stayed in New Orleans. I moved back, and I stayed there. We had a gig at a place called the [Crescent City] Brewhouse in 1990 to 1991. It was a nine month gig. We played every weekend. It was the only one of its kind. They had modern jazz two nights a week.
It’s right downtown in the French Quarter. It’s on Decatur Street, right across from Jackson Brewery

It’s still there, but we – the management, they said that they wanted to have a jazz establishment, but they didn’t. They just wanted music to be background for their patrons. They gave us a space. We did our own advertising. We had some good gigs up in there. Now they just have a couple of guys playing under the staircase, things like that.
